title: Phantom Edges in Phantom Blade Zero - the 16 With a Recorded Location
description: All 16 Phantom Edges in Phantom Blade Zero - cannons, spears, axes and instruments rather than more swords - with where each is found and how they pair with blades.
keyword: phantom edge phantom blade zero, secondary weapons phantom blade zero, all phantom edges

sections.title: What Phantom Edges Are
sections.content:
Phantom Edges occupy Soul's two secondary weapon slots. The set is deliberately ungovernable - cannons, spears, shields, bows and an instrument - which is a long way from a standard sword list. The word “Edge” in the name is doing conceptual work rather than literal work: several of them are not blades at all.

16 Phantom Edges have a recorded acquisition point, against an official total of around 25. They cover problems a blade build cannot - range, reach, and a couple of utility answers like thread-cutting - which is why a loadout is a choice about which situations you can handle rather than a damage comparison.

sections.title: How Many Phantom Edges Are There, Really?
sections.content:
Two numbers circulate and they are not the same number. The launch acquisition table behind this page records 16. The Chinese BWIKI catalogue that predates release listed 33 names, splitting them into 23 it considered confirmed and 10 it could not place - and warned in writing that some of the unplaced names were not official at all.

Neither number is a mistake. The BWIKI list is a name catalogue collected before release, so it includes entries that were cut, renamed or never shipped. This page lists what a named source ties to an acquisition point, because a name with no location cannot be found in the game. If a missing edge turns up with a verified route, it is one record in src/data/entities/weapons.json and it appears here on the next build.

sections.title: The Types, and Why They Exist
sections.content:
Types are read off the item name where the name states one; the rest are marked “not stated” rather than inferred from a screenshot.

  • Cannons and bows - the ranged answer. Tiger Cannon is a boss drop, Feather Bow is an early outpost pickup.
  • Spears and tridents - reach on a melee weapon.
  • Axes and polearms - slow, heavy, guard-breaking.
  • Throwing blades - Flying Dagger and Flying Guillotine, both cheap to get and easy to forget to equip.
  • The pipa - an instrument, and the only entry whose attacks are not obviously strikes.

sections.title: Pairing With Blades
sections.content: Two blades plus two Phantom Edges, all four live during a fight. Swapping between them refills stamina and continues the combo chain, so a run is normally built around which two edges cover what the blades cannot.

sections.title: Source Status
sections.content: Tier-2 index generated from src/data/entities/weapons.json. See the weapons hub.

sections.title: What They Do In A Fight
sections.content:
Each use consumes 残魂星火 - BWIKI glosses this as Remnant Spark - in amounts that vary per edge, and the resource is refunded probabilistically by killing enemies. So edges are not a free ability: they are an expenditure you sustain by fighting, which is a different economy from the Sha-chi bar that governs your heavy attacks and guarding.

Combat uses the source lists: some edges break the defence of giant-shield enemies (攻克巨盾敌人防御), several counter specific enemies outright, and edges can be woven into combos, used for pursuit attacks, or trigger scene-specific interactions. You carry two and can swap between them at any time.

Outside combat they are the keyring for the map: an axe smashes environmental barriers, a chain sickle works as a grappling hook, and areas needing a particular edge are marked on the map - see collectibles for how gated pickups are tracked.

Count discrepancy, stated plainly. Official material has announced 25 Phantom Edges; BWIKI's catalogue reaches 33 rows counting its own unconfirmed list. That gap is not a contradiction to resolve here - it is the difference between a publisher total and a fan wiki's working inventory of everything it has spotted in footage. Neither number is verification of the other.
